Net -3 names (falsifier 10 on bus-completion: a build adds no net new vocabulary). THE SEAM PROVED, AND THE RUNG MEASURED UNRUN. Working item 1 of the build order ('wire the gate') began by verifying its stated blocker — 'wiring needs a live system_rackmount instance the harbor can reach' — and found it false: ask() is a plain method on the device, no bus, no daemon, no instance. proofs/test_harbor_asks_the_real_host.py (5 teeth, green, sealed under a real netns) now puts the REAL SystemRackmountDevice behind clear(resources=...): every HARBOR_LINES name is a probe the device advertises on the ask door; the device's own predicate drives the refusal in BOTH directions (cpu crosses up, memory crosses down); the refusal names the harbor's line and never the device's reading, in the message text too; and a quiet box clears, recorded. Teeth mutation-checked. AND THE LARGER FACT UNDERNEATH: 0 of 229 journaled records across 21 histories carry cleared_by — no crossing in the system's recorded life has passed this rung, and clear() has no production caller at all. That is this charter's own falsifier condition ('if devices advance workflows AROUND it once the clearance gate lands, the authority rung has failed') met continuously since the gate was built. Filed: CairnCommons/troubles/every-crossing-goes-around-the-clearance-gate.json. Wiring resources= was never the missing step; a caller is.

THE REGISTRY IS OUT; PROVEN-SPACE IS A TRAVERSAL. Akien: 'methodregistry is a registry. generally we frown on registries. why do we need one here?' — then 'rip out the registry now, before item 2.' MEASURED before cutting: clearance.py was its ONLY consumer and it DISCARDED the callable resolve() returned, so the one thing a registry uniquely gives (name -> object) served nobody; filed_edges named no future consumer. PROVENANCE: registry.py's header said 'RE-INSTATED, NOT RE-DERIVED (Law 1)' — it came back from the ground_loop driver-executor, which DISPATCHED and so genuinely needed the map; that executor role was called a goof and stripped, and the registry returned with its map intact and its question moved. Law 1 forbids re-deriving a settled answer; it does not license carrying one forward past its question. WHAT LANDED: registry.py DELETED. clear() takes `proven_by` — the proof's own path — and asks tester/validation_store.standing(), which reads the seal already sitting at the derived address (proofs/x.py -> validations/x.json). No second in-memory copy of a fact that attaches at its own endpoint (Law 6). UnprovenMethod -> Unproven, and the rename IS the design change: the gate no longer asks about a named method, it asks about CODE. THE GATE GAINED WHAT THE CACHE COULD NOT HAVE: every VALIDATION has promised for three weeks that it is 'valid until the proof file or the code it proves changes' and nothing checked it. source_fingerprint (one sha256 over every *.py under the component root — the horizon's own scope, path+content, deliberately NOT git so a seal expires when the working tree diverges, not when someone commits) is recorded by the tester inside `evidence` at seal time, never as a ninth field, and standing() recomputes it at read time. A green seal whose code has moved underneath it is now REFUSED (Law 3). Four new teeth in test_clearance.py replace the two registry ones — never-sealed, sealed-then-RED, horizon-closed, and the record naming the proof it leaned on — over REAL scratch component trees run by the REAL tester and landed through the REAL write-door. The horizon tooth edits a SIBLING module, not the proof, and pre-checks that the same component cleared BEFORE the edit, so it cannot pass vacuously; two mutations (fingerprint scoped to the proof only; the comparison short-circuited) each turn it red. SIDE EFFECT WORTH NAMING: validation_store had 73 trails on disk and ZERO readers — every seal written, none ever consulted. standing() is the first reader, and harbor_master's own two proofs are the first two nodes in the corpus whose proven-space is DERIVED rather than asserted. Pre-existing seals carry no fingerprint and therefore read NOT proven ('Unknown is not green', Law 9) until re-run — which is the honest answer, not a regression. Also fixed in passing: cairn/tester/proofs/test_scratch.py was RED before this session with four proofs reaching tempfile.mkdtemp directly; my two new ones would have been six. All six now use cairn.tester.scratch.scratch_dir and that proof is green — 'pre-existing' is not a disposition.

note: THE VOYAGE OPENS UNDER A CHARTED COURSE AND A CONFIRMED RULING. The chart chain berthed all seven stages this session (orient -> validate); the validate berth carrying the acceptance criteria is /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/validate-20260810T181604-6a91af792939.json. The design question this ticket cast as its GATING child (a) — 'where a boat carries its owner' — is ANSWERED BY RULING rather than by build: decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal, in which Akien settled that an INTENTION owns its TICKET, a ticket owns its WORKFLOW, and the workflow IS the boat. So the voyage is smaller than it was cast, and this crossing is where that is first recorded. WHAT THE CHART FOUND THAT THE CAST DID NOT KNOW, and which reshaped the build: the two fields a ticket already carries are both SPOKEN FOR — the store's own template declares `intention` as the WHAT and `owner` as the mover, and a census over 100 filed tickets confirms both live up to their declarations. So the owning intention is a new field, not a re-reading; overloading either would be keeping a word and replacing what fills it, which is the exact failure that produced this ticket.

workflow: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME:waiting] -> WATCHME(boat-owner-comes-from-the-boat) -> PROVED
note: THE OWNER IS READ OFF THE BOAT, AND THIS CROSSING IS THE FIRST ONE TO USE IT. clear() no longer takes boat_owner; it resolves boat_id -> CairnCommons/tickets/<id>.json -> owning_intention -> that charter -> gated_by, files only, and compares the actor by EXACT LIST MEMBERSHIP. The comparison changed SHAPE, not just its source: a hand is never equal to an intention, it is ADMITTED BY one — Law 6's second clause rather than its first. WHAT WAS REFUSED ON PURPOSE, because each is the same hole wearing a coat: clear() accepts no tickets_dir= (root injection would hand the caller back the choice of what the gate reads); a boat_owner= keyword RAISES rather than riding **journal_extra into the record (removing the parameter alone would have left that door open, and a forged field in a record of truth is worse than a bad argument); mint_grant reads the boat too, so a caller cannot mint itself standing from an owner it invented; and boat_id must agree with the ticket the gates read, which until now could disagree. Four routes, because the ticket's falsifier clause (1) is 'the same hole wearing a different field' and one closed door is not a closed room. TWO NEW DECLARED FIELDS, NEITHER BACK-FILLED: owning_intention on the tickets template, distinguished from `intention` and `owner` BY SHAPE (this one resolves; those are prose — measured over 100 filed tickets), and gated_by on harbor_master's charter ALONE, grown against need, because 22 of 24 beside-code charters carry an `owner` over 60 characters and 2 carry an empty one, so matching an actor against that prose is a substring scan — a check that goes green for the wrong reason. The fleet-wide fill and the who-may-mint question are filed as an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands and cited by address from the code, so the debt and the code point at each other. SIX NEW TEETH, 21 green twice and sealed under netns. The reach tooth was written WRONG TWICE and both versions are recorded in it: too narrow collected only cairn.* names so four forbidden terms could never match, too wide swept in the tester and went red over somebody else's correct shelling out. A tooth that fires on normal motion gets silenced, and silencing is how a real signal is trained away. NON-HOLLOW BY REVERT, both directions run: an actor naming itself owner of a boat it does not own PASSES the authority rung on reverted code and is REFUSED on built code. The ticket's own falsifier was AMBIGUOUS about that sign and the ambiguity is recorded beside it rather than written over — the original wording is the evidence that this happens.

build_gate: clean — build_inspector ran 19 sieves over harbor_master
note: THE WATCH IS ARMED, AND WHAT IT WATCHES CANNOT BE BOUGHT WITH VOLUME. The build is done and green; the claim it cannot settle is whether the read made the Law 6 refusal BIND, because every crossing in this system is made by one hand and a gate that admits exactly that hand is indistinguishable from a gate that admits everyone. Falsifier clause (3) — every boat's owner resolving to one string — is ALREADY TRUE at n=2 and no amount of building escapes it here. So the probe's `enough` requires a SECOND DISTINCT ACTOR on a cleared crossing, expressed as len(distinct_actors) >= 2 rather than as 'not CC': hard-coding the hand would strand a learned value in a human's head and go stale the day a second device is named. Its trigger's condition (a) — a cleared crossing whose actor the boat does not admit — has no sample floor, because one record proves it and waiting for twenty would be waiting to confirm what the first showed. Condition (b) is falsifier clause (3) as a trend, and it requires the corpus to collapse on BOTH axes at once (one owning intention AND one actor), since one intention moving many boats is ordinary and so is one hand moving many intentions' boats. THE PROBE RE-RESOLVES RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE RECORD: the crossing records cleared_by and actor but not the owner the gate resolved, so it opens the boat again and asks whether that actor is admitted — a record carrying the resolved owner would be the gate grading its own homework. Era floor 18:00, between the last crossing cleared by the defective comparison (16:55:29) and this voyage's; those two records stand and are not counted as evidence about their own fix (Law 7). THE VERDICT WAS WRITTEN AND DEPOSITED BEFORE THIS CROSSING: 8 criteria passing, 11 hypotheses dispositioned, one of them a PARTIAL KILL — the prediction that a cleared crossing would honestly read delegated=True is false, because transitions.py:749 renders that field on the standing line, so a constant would mark every crossing delegated and inform nobody. The reasoning was sound and argued for a second field, not for redefining this one.

For a year the sentence harbor_master's charter rests on — an actor who is not the boat's owner and holds no grant is refused — was real code that ran and returned the answer its caller asked for, because `actor` and `boat_owner` arrived from the same hand in the same call. FOUR ROUTES WERE CLOSED, NOT ONE, because the ticket's own falsifier clause (1) is 'the same hole wearing a different field': the parameter is gone; a boat_owner= keyword RAISES instead of riding **journal_extra into a record of truth (removing the parameter alone would have left that open, and a forged field in a record is worse than a bad argument); mint_grant reads the boat too, so no caller mints itself standing from an owner it invented; and boat_id must agree with the ticket the gates read, which until today could disagree. NON-HOLLOW BY REVERT, BOTH DIRECTIONS: the exploit call PASSES the authority rung on reverted code and is REFUSED on built code — and the ticket's own falsifier was AMBIGUOUS about which way that points, so the unambiguous statement is recorded beside the original rather than written over it, the original being the evidence that this happens at all. Consequence accepted: proofs must name REAL boats, so the fixtures are live ticket ids and _OWNER is derived by reading rather than written down. The fleet-wide fill and the who-may-mint hole are FILED as an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands and cited by address from the code, filed before the teeth rather than after, because a known hole placed after the conformers is how it becomes folklore. A TOOTH WRITTEN WRONG TWICE IS RECORDED IN ITSELF: the reach check was first too narrow (a set that by construction held only cairn.* names, so four forbidden terms were decoration) and then too wide (it swept in the tester and went red over somebody else's correct shelling out — a tooth that fires on normal motion gets silenced, and silencing is how a real signal is trained away). WHAT THIS BUILD CANNOT SETTLE, carried by an instrument instead of an argument: whether the refusal binds anything. One hand moves everything here, so the probe's `enough` demands a second actor and no volume of CC crossings reaches it. That is the honest edge of this voyage, and it is the same edge the ticket named at cast rather than one discovered late.
